newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-U.S.FAVOURITES FOR WORLD CUP DESPITE LINE-UP CHANGE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-U.S.FAVOURITES FOR WORLD CUP DESPITE LINE-UP CHANGE.

text.p: The United States will start as favourites for the 1996 World Cup of Golf on Thursday, even though four-time winners Fred Couples and Davis Love III are both missing this year's event.

In world number two and reigning British Open champion Tom Lehman and close friend and U.S. Open title-holder Steve Jones, they possess the strongest line-up in a tournament noticeably weakened by the absence of many of the game's top players.

Apart from Lehman, only South Africa's Ernie Els (number four), Zimbabwe's Nick Price (12) and Germany's Bernhard Langer (15) are among the current world top 20 who will be competing at the Erinvale Golf Club.

Lehman comes to South Africa on top of his form. Victory in last weekend's Grand Slam of Golf by two shots over World Cup partner Jones keeps the man from Scottsdale, Arizona in second place on the Sony rankings. He also currently heads the U.S. team standings for next year's Ryder Cup from U.S. PGA champion Mark Brooks.
Steve Jones is ranked 30th in the world and the U.S. are widely tipped to improve on their impressive World Cup record of 21 team victories in 41 appearances.
"I think we'll make a good team because Steve is such a good friend," says Lehman. "I can't think of anybody I'd rather play with, so it will be a great week."
Jones believes that playing for his country in the World Cup is "something extra special".
"I know some of the great players in the game have represented the United States and now it is nice to be part of that history," he said.

Host country South Africa, represented by three-time world matchplay champion Ernie Els and big-hitting Wayne Westner, are also expected to feature prominently in the 32-team event. They will be aiming for a third World Cup victory after wins by Gary Player and Harold Henning in 1965 and by Dale Hayes and Bobby Cole in 1974.

Els arrives back in the land of his birth fresh from victory in Asia's Johnnie Walker Super Tour while Westner finished joint second in his last two tournaments, the Volvo Masters and the Moroccan Open.

Of the other seeded nations playing 72 holes of strokeplay golf over the picturesque par-72 layout just outside Cape Town, Zimbabwe, Germany, Scotland and Ireland are all realistic challengers for the trophy.

Zimbabwe, who finished second to Couples and Love III in both 1993 and 1994, are represented by South African tour regulars Mark McNulty and Tony Johnstone while Germany -- World Cup winners in 1990 -- will be spearheaded for the 10th time by Bernhard Langer who has 1995 Volvo Masters champion Alexander Cejka as his partner.

Scotland field two of their victorious 1995 Dunhill Cup trio in the experienced Sam Torrance and Andrew Coltart and Ireland's hopes are carried by 1996 Spanish Open winner Padraig Harrington and reigning German Masters champion Darren Clarke -- two of he brightest young talents on the European tour.
